hypothesis: The agent only ever uses Bash (20 of 20 tool calls in run 4a6d16; the system prompt already says Read/Edit are not needed), yet 22 other tool definitions (Task, Cron*, Worktree, Monitor, NotebookEdit, WebFetch, Workflow, etc.) plus the skill listing are sent and re-read on every call. Restricting the toolset to Bash removes that fixed overhead from every call, which is a mechanism that lowers tokens on every run regardless of noise in call count.
changeSummary: Set claudeCode.tools to ["Bash"] in config.json (complete claudeCode block kept: systemPromptMode append + tools). No other change; system-prompt.md is unchanged.

evidence: run-20261115-184425-4a6d16 profile: fixed system+tools ≈11.8k/call, re-read over later calls ≈236k (23% of 1.10M). Init message lists 23 tools and 17 skills, and the profile flags "22/23 tool definitions loaded but never used; used: Bash". Same pattern in the other exp-0002 runs (13-26 calls, first-call context 18.2k in all of them). Calls are 13-26 per run, so any per-call cut multiplies. Most failures seen (api.bookmark.boost, startup.app evaluator disk error in fd077f) are unrelated to tools. The 999k run failed only because of an evaluator infra error (no free disk).
expectedSavings: Tool schemas for the 22 unused tools plus the skill/agent listings are plausibly 5-8k tokens of the 11.8k fixed overhead. Over a median ~21 calls that is about 105-170k tokens, roughly 10-15% of 1.10M. The cache-read price is paid on every call, and a smaller prefix also shrinks the cache-write on call 1. Risk: if the harness rejects the tools field format, or Bash-only makes the agent's heredoc edits less reliable, calls could increase. The prompt already instructs Bash-only, and all 20 calls in the sampled run were Bash. Run-to-run noise of about 30% still applies.
